title: Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject
source_text: The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request. That period may be extended by two further months where necessary, taking into account the complexity and number of the requests. The controller shall inform the data subject of any such extension within one month of receipt of the request, together with the reasons for the delay. Where the data subject makes the request by electronic form means, the information shall be provided by electronic means where possible, unless otherwise requested by the data subject.
action: [1] provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 to the data subject || [2] extend the response period by two further months || [3] inform the data subject of any such extension, together with the reasons for the delay || [4] provide the information by electronic means
condition_constraint_exception: [1] condition: request under Articles 15 to 22 has been received; constraint: without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request; exception: null || [2] condition: where necessary, taking into account the complexity and number of the requests; constraint: extension of two further months only; exception: null || [3] condition: the period is extended; constraint: within one month of receipt of the request; exception: null || [4] condition: the data subject makes the request by electronic form means; constraint: where possible; exception: unless otherwise requested by the data subject
scope_qualifier: [1] kind: exception; text: electronic-means duty does not apply if the data subject requests otherwise; applies_to: [4]; evidence: unless otherwise requested by the data subject || [2] kind: scope; text: covers requests by the data subject under Articles 15 to 22; applies_to: [1]; evidence: a request under Articles 15 to 22
evidence_quote: [1] The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request || [2] That period may be extended by two further months where necessary, taking into account the complexity and number of the requests || [3] The controller shall inform the data subject of any such extension within one month of receipt of the request, together with the reasons for the delay || [4] Where the data subject makes the request by electronic form means, the information shall be provided by electronic means where possible, unless otherwise requested by the data subject
uncertainty_notes: [2] and [4] are passive ('may be extended', 'shall be provided') so no actor is named; the controller is obviously meant but I left actor null per the guideline (no inferring). 'where possible' in [4] treated as a constraint, not an exception. Split the extension permission [2] from the extension-notice duty [3] because the effect and modality differ.

title: Data protection by design and by default
source_text: Taking into account the state of the art, the cost of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity for rights and freedoms of natural persons posed by the processing, the controller shall, both at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, which are designed to implement data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, in an effective manner and to integrate the necessary safeguards into the processing in order to meet the requirements of this Regulation and protect the rights of data subjects.
action: [1] implement appropriate technical and organisational measures (e.g. pseudonymisation) designed to implement data-protection principles (e.g. data minimisation) effectively and to integrate necessary safeguards into the processing
condition_constraint_exception: [1] condition: null; constraint: at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself; taking into account the state of the art, cost of implementation, nature, scope, context and purposes of processing and the risks of varying likelihood and severity to rights and freedoms; in order to meet the requirements of the Regulation and protect the rights of data subjects; exception: null
evidence_quote: [1] the controller shall, both at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures
uncertainty_notes: Single duty. 'Taking into account...' is a standard governing how the measures are chosen, so I put it under constraint rather than as an exception or scope qualifier. 'such as pseudonymisation / data minimisation' are examples only, not separate duties.

title: Conditions for consent
source_text: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time. The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal. Prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed thereof. It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.
action: [1] withdraw his or her consent || [2] inform the data subject of the right to withdraw consent || [3] make withdrawal of consent as easy as giving consent
condition_constraint_exception: [1] condition: null; constraint: at any time; exception: withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal || [2] condition: prior to giving consent; constraint: null; exception: null || [3] condition: null; constraint: as easy to withdraw as to give consent; exception: null
scope_qualifier: [1] kind: exception; text: withdrawal is not retroactive: it does not affect lawfulness of processing based on consent before withdrawal; applies_to: [1]; evidence: The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal
evidence_quote: [1] The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time || [2] Prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed thereof || [3] It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent
uncertainty_notes: 'Shall have the right' = MAY (a right, not a duty). The non-retroactivity sentence has no actor and does not require or forbid an act, so I treated it as a qualifier on [1] only. [2] and [3] are passive; actor left null even though the controller is implied. 'thereof' in [2] read as the right to withdraw (the preceding sentence).

title: Right to object
source_text: The data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her which is based on point (e) or (f) of Article 6(1), including profiling based on those provisions. The controller shall no longer process the personal data unless the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds for the processing which override the interests, rights and freedoms of the data subject or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.
action: [1] object to processing of personal data concerning him or her based on Article 6(1)(e) or (f), including profiling based on those provisions || [2] process the personal data
condition_constraint_exception: [1] condition: on grounds relating to his or her particular situation; constraint: at any time; exception: null || [2] condition: the data subject has objected (from "no longer process"); constraint: null; exception: unless the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds for the processing which override the interests, rights and freedoms of the data subject, or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims
scope_qualifier: [1] kind: scope; text: right applies only to processing based on Article 6(1)(e) or (f), including profiling based on those provisions; applies_to: [1]; evidence: which is based on point (e) or (f) of Article 6(1), including profiling based on those provisions || [2] kind: exception; text: controller may continue processing if it demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds overriding the data subject, or for legal claims; applies_to: [2]; evidence: unless the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds for the processing which override the interests, rights and freedoms of the data subject or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims
evidence_quote: [1] The data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to his or her particular situation, at any time to processing of personal data concerning him or her which is based on point (e) or (f) of Article 6(1), including profiling based on those provisions || [2] The controller shall no longer process the personal data
uncertainty_notes: 'No longer process' is a prohibition (MUST_NOT) and implies an objection has been made; I recorded that as the condition because the text itself ties 'no longer' to the objection. The burden is on the controller to 'demonstrate' the override: recorded in the exception, not a separate duty.

source_text: A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only in accordance with the provisions of this Act and for a lawful purpose,— (a) for which the Data Principal has given her consent; or (b) for certain legitimate uses.
action: [1] process the personal data of a Data Principal
condition_constraint_exception: [1] condition: for a lawful purpose: (a) for which the Data Principal has given her consent; or (b) for certain legitimate uses; constraint: only in accordance with the provisions of this Act and for a lawful purpose; exception: null
evidence_quote: [1] A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only in accordance with the provisions of this Act and for a lawful purpose
uncertainty_notes: Hard call on modality: the text says 'may ... only', which works as a restriction (could be read as MUST_NOT process otherwise). The guideline says preserve source polarity and not turn a permission into something else, so I kept MAY and put the 'only' limit under constraint. Consent / legitimate uses are the two alternative lawful grounds (condition). 'certain legitimate uses' is not defined in this chunk.

source_text: A Data Fiduciary shall, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary or failure of General a Data Principal to carry out the duties provided under this Act, be responsible for complying obligations of Data with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder in respect of any processing Fiduciary. undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor.

uncertainty_notes: Source text is garbled: the marginal heading 'General obligations of Data Fiduciary.' is interleaved into the sentence ('failure of General a Data Principal', 'complying obligations of Data with', 'processing Fiduciary. undertaken'). I read it as 'be responsible for complying with the provisions...'. Evidence quotes are copied exactly as garbled so they still match the source. 'Irrespective of any agreement...' is not an exception, it blocks exceptions, so I put it under constraint.

source_text: Where personal data processed by a Data Fiduciary is likely to be— (a) used to make a decision that affects the Data Principal; or (b) disclosed to another Data Fiduciary, the Data Fiduciary processing such personal data shall ensure its completeness, accuracy and consistency.

uncertainty_notes: One duty with two alternative triggers (a)/(b), so one record. Completeness/accuracy/consistency are the object of 'ensure', not three duties.

source_text: Every request for consent under the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder shall be presented to the Data Principal in a clear and plain language, giving her the option to access such request in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution and providing the contact details of a Data Protection Officer, where applicable, or of any other person authorised by the Data Fiduciary to respond to any communication from the Data Principal for the purpose of exercise of her rights under the provisions of this Act.

Could reasonably be one record with three constraints. The sentence uses a passive ('shall be presented'), so no actor is named; 'Data Fiduciary' only appears inside the third item, so I left actor null. 'where applicable' attached to the DPO limb only.

title: Notice given by Data Fiduciary to Data Principal
source_text: The notice given by the Data Fiduciary to the Data Principal shall— be presented and be understandable independently of any other information that has been, is or may be made available by such Data Fiduciary;
action: [1] present the notice so that it is understandable independently of any other information made available by the Data Fiduciary

uncertainty_notes: Chunk is only item (a) of a list: the lead-in 'The notice ... shall—' supplies the modality. Actor: the grammatical subject is 'the notice', but it is 'given by the Data Fiduciary', so I recorded Data Fiduciary as the responsible actor. Other items of the rule are not in this chunk.

title: Registration and obligations of Consent Manager
source_text: A person who fulfils the conditions for registration of Consent Managers set out in Part A of First Schedule may apply to the Board for registration as a Consent Manager by furnishing such particulars and such other information and documents as the Board may publish in this behalf on its website.

uncertainty_notes: Express permission, so outcome = obligations. 'as the Board may publish' just describes what the applicant must furnish; I did not treat it as a separate permission for the Board. Part A conditions themselves are not in this chunk.

title: Intimation of personal data breach
source_text: On becoming aware of any personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall, to the best of its knowledge, intimate to each affected Data Principal, in a concise, clear and plain manner and without delay, through her user account or any mode of communication registered by her with the Data Fiduciary, — (a) a description of the breach, including its nature, extent and the timing of its occurrence; (b) the consequences relevant to her, that are likely to arise from the breach; (c) the measures implemented and being implemented by the Data Fiduciary, if any, to mitigate risk; (d) the safety measures that she may take to protect her interests; and (e) business contact information of a person who is able to respond on behalf of the Data Fiduciary, to queries, if any, of the Data Principal.
action: [1] intimate each affected Data Principal of the personal data breach, including (a) description of the breach (nature, extent, timing), (b) likely consequences relevant to her, (c) mitigation measures implemented and being implemented, (d) safety measures she may take, (e) business contact information of a person who can respond to queries
condition_constraint_exception: [1] condition: on becoming aware of any personal data breach; constraint: to the best of its knowledge; in a concise, clear and plain manner; without delay; through her user account or any mode of communication registered by her with the Data Fiduciary; exception: null

uncertainty_notes: Items (a)-(e) are the contents of one intimation, not separate duties, so one record. 'if any' in (c) and 'if any' queries in (e) are minor limits inside the content list. Timing: 'without delay' only, no fixed deadline in this chunk.

title: Verifiable consent for processing of personal data of child
source_text: A Data Fiduciary shall adopt appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure that verifiable consent of the parent is obtained before the processing of any personal data of a child and shall observe due diligence, for checking that the individual identifying herself as the parent is an adult who is identifiable if required in connection with compliance with any law for the time being in force in India, by reference to— (a) reliable details of identity and age of the individual available with the Data Fiduciary; or (b) details of identity and age, voluntarily provided — (i) by the individual; or (ii) through a virtual token mapped to such details, which is issued by an authorised entity.

data_category: [1] personal data of a child || [2] details of identity and age of the individual claiming to be the parent
condition_constraint_exception: [1] condition: before the processing of any personal data of a child; constraint: null; exception: null || [2] condition: if required in connection with compliance with any law for the time being in force in India (applies to the identifiability check); constraint: by reference to (a) reliable details of identity and age available with the Data Fiduciary, or (b) details of identity and age voluntarily provided (i) by the individual or (ii) through a virtual token mapped to such details issued by an authorised entity; exception: null

uncertainty_notes: Two duties joined by 'and' with different acts (adopt measures vs due-diligence check), so two records. Not sure the 'if required...' condition governs only 'identifiable' or the whole due-diligence check; I read it as attached to 'identifiable' (closest antecedent). Data category for [2] is the identity/age detail used for verification, stated in the text.

source_text: A business that controls the collection of a consumer’s personal information shall, at or before the point of collection, inform consumers of the following: The categories of personal information to be collected and the purposes for which the categories of personal information are collected or used and whether that information is sold or shared. A business shall not collect additional categories of personal information or use personal information collected for additional purposes that are incompatible with the disclosed purpose for which the personal information was collected without providing the consumer with notice consistent with this section.
actor: [1] business that controls the collection of a consumer’s personal information || [2] business || [3] business

'Without providing ... notice' is modelled as an exception to both prohibitions. The 'of the following' list is in this chunk's first sentence, folded into [1].

uncertainty_notes: This is a duty to disclose the deletion right, not the grant of the right itself, so I did not add a MAY record for the consumer. The manner of disclosure is in Section 1798.130 (not in this chunk).

source_text: A consumer shall have the right to request that a business that collects personal information about the consumer disclose to the consumer the following: (1) The categories of personal information it has collected about that consumer. (2) The categories of sources from which the personal information is collected. (3) The business or commercial purpose for collecting, selling, or sharing personal information. (4) The categories of third parties to whom the business discloses personal information. (5) The specific pieces of personal information it has collected about that consumer.

action: [1] provide a clear and conspicuous link on the business’ internet homepages, titled “Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information,” to an internet web page that enables a consumer, or a person authorized by the consumer, to opt out of the sale or sharing of the consumer’s personal information

uncertainty_notes: Only the first item (the homepage link) of the list is in this chunk, so one record.
